results.title: Eggs: Are they good or bad for my cholesterol? - Mayo Clinic
results.snippet: One large egg has about 186 mg of cholesterol — all of which is found in the yolk. If your diet contains little other cholesterol, according to some studies, eating up to an egg a day might be an OK choice. If you like eggs but don't want the cholesterol, use only the egg whites.

results.title: Are Eggs Bad for Cholesterol? What the Science Says | Cedars-Sinai
results.snippet: Does eating eggs raise blood cholesterol levels? A healthy total blood cholesterol level ranges from 140 to 200mg/dl.One egg per day is unlikely to significantly increase your cholesterol or your risk for cardiovascular disease. Eat eggs the Heart-Healthy Way.
